answer.evidence: The crystal on top is decor. The pedestal cap spans rows 12-15 and is wider than the shaft (14 vs 8). A lighter front-edge line at row 15 (L=197) is followed by the dark brown band at rows 16-19. The shaft below (rows 16-25) is a vertical face and tapers 12, 10, 8. The base steps out again at rows 26-29 (width 12-14), with a lighter line at row 28 and darker rows 29-30. The cap is a chamfered rectangular slab rather than a true ellipse. Its widths run 12, 14, 14, 14, 14, then 12 and 12, which is not a clear widen-then-narrow profile. So rounded_at_both_edges is false, but a top band with an edge line is still present.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small crystal on a grey pedestal. Its dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a neutral dark line rather than a tinted dark material tone. The pedestal reads as about 3 grey steps with a flat body and a dark outline, which is the sticker look. The crystal has a few facet tones, but its surfaces carry no grain, speckle or per-stone shading. At 9 visible tones per tile it matches the hedge, but it falls well short of the well (20) and the cheese stall (17), which are the richer same-kind props. Near-flat coverage of 17% is above every reference except the stall at 13%, so there are flat areas. Overall it looks thinner and flatter than the Beodeul props.
